title: Introduce observability query proxy and token-cost facade
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds obs-query-proxy service to provide a low-latency query API that stitches metrics, traces and logs into a per-invocation token-cost breakdown; new Console endpoints and dashboards; minor alert tuning to account for the new telemetry. No user-visible API-breaking changes.
commits: initial scaffold of obs-query-proxy service and API surface
implement token-cost facade and KV cache joiners
docs, helm chart and dashboard wiring; tests and lint fixes
body:
Summary: Adds a thin service (obs-query-proxy) that provides a query-time facade to stitch together metrics, spans and sampled logs into a compact per-invocation breakdown that Console and SLO tooling can consume. Motivation: customers and platform teams frequently need fast, single-request slices of telemetry for a given invocation id or timewindow for triage and billing reconciliation. Existing APIs require multiple queries and expensive joins client-side. This PR introduces a low-latency proxy that performs safe server-side joins, caches recent invocation joins, and exposes a token-cost facade optimized for the Console and alerting workflows.

What changed (high level):
- New service: services/obs-query-proxy. Lightweight HTTP+gRPC layer with auth middleware. Handles invocation id -> metrics + spans + log snippet joins. Includes request-level permissive rate limits and tenant scoping.
- Token-cost facade: pkg/observability/token_cost_facade.go computes a per-invocation decomposition across model compute, kv-cache hits, network, and queueing time. Outputs both absolute cost-estimates and normalized per-token contributions (P50/P90).
- Tracing and sampling: small changes in pkg/otel/spans.go to add a 'obs.query.proxy' span kind and to pass invocation anchors into sampled log collectors.
- Console integration: console/api/obs_query_routes.go exposes two routes: /api/obs/query and /api/obs/invocation/{id}/cost. Dashboard JSON added for token_cost_facet to show per-invocation waterfall and sparkline.
- Deploy: helm chart + values for deploying obs-query-proxy in Dedicated and Private.
- Tests: e2e and unit tests added (tests/e2e/obs_query_proxy_test.go) that exercise tenant isolation and cache eviction semantics.
- Docs: docs/observability/query-proxy.md with design rationale, SLA expectations and runbook for incidents.

Implementation notes:
- The proxy performs read-only joins using existing metric indices and the sampled-trace store; there is no new long-term retention index. Joins are bounded by a configurable result size and cutoff to avoid expensive scans.
- Cache: in-memory LRU for recent invocation joins + optional Redis-backed mode for Dedicated. Cache keys include tenant + invocation id + model-version tag.
- Cost model: conservative heuristics derived from per-kernel time-weighting and per-GPU unit-cost. This is explicitly documented as an estimate and flagged in API responses. We emit a sample-level uncertainty field so consumers can decide whether to trust estimates for billing vs triage.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4321)
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] E2E tests for tenant isolation and cache correctness
- [x] Basic load test run on staging (sustained 250 RPS with 95th P90 < 120ms for cached lookups)
- [x] Docs and Console wiring
- [x] Helm chart

Review commentary (abridged):
- Diego Morales: "Nice separation. Two asks: make cache TTL configurable per-tenant and ensure the proxy doesn't expose internal metric names in the API response. Also add a high-cardinality attack mitigation (denylist by app id)."
- Asha (author): "Addressed: added tenant-specific TTL config and a response field mapping layer that hides internal index names. Denylist support was added to the auth middleware; see services/obs-query-proxy/main.go lines 140-200."
- Lars Öberg: "Perf nit: the join logic currently performs a small number of sequential queries; if SLO sensitive we should parallelize dependent reads. Also please add a circuit-breaker for trace-store timeouts."
- Asha: "Parallelized the metrics + trace read path and added a context deadline + Circuit breaker fallback to return partial results with a 'partial: true' marker. Tests updated."
- Priya Singh: "Security: confirm RBAC for tenant-scoped queries and add a small e2e that attempts cross-tenant read."
- Asha: "Added e2e case (tests/e2e/obs_query_proxy_test.go::CrossTenantIsolation) and verified logs show denied access attempts (good coverage)."

CI and validation: initial CI run flagged a lint failure and a flaky e2e. Fixed the lint issues (gofmt and typo in docs) and stabilized the e2e by tightening the test timing and adding a health-check wait. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, e2e, lint, build image).

Backward compatibility and risk:
- No breaking API changes to existing public telemetry collectors. The new Console routes are additive.
- The cost estimates are explicitly labeled as approximate; we made this conservative to avoid billing surprises.
- Operational risk: additional service to run. We included a minimal SLO and alerting baseline in the chart (high error-rate alarm + latency P95 > 2s alarm).

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-20 after approvals from Diego, Lars and Priya. Deploy plan: staged rollout to staging (2 nodes) for 48h then gradual rollout to Dedicated clusters with telemetry gating. Runbook: docs/observability/query-proxy.md#runbook

Notes for oncall: If the proxy induces increased load on the trace-store, the circuit breaker will start returning partial responses. Monitor obs.query_proxy.trace_timeouts and obs.query_proxy.cache_hit_ratio. If partial responses exceed 10% for >10 minutes, revert to previous release using the helm rollback documented in the runbook.
